evidence.text: The character-specific entry gives 令’s Mandarin pinyin as lìng. Its cited dictionary senses include issuing commands, an order, and causing or allowing. This verifies the ordinary current reading lìng; it does not establish which reading the 令 phonetic element had in 零.

search_audit.query: site:unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=96F6 零 kMandarin líng; site:unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=4EE4 令 kMandarin lìng; 令 lìng 零 líng Mandarin pronunciation dictionary official
search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced Taiwan MOE character-specific records and Unicode lookup URLs. Opened the MOE 令 page and confirmed lìng; the 零 page timed out, though its search result reported líng and lián. Both required official character-specific Unicode records were attempted and inaccessible. Local full Unihan rows were checked for both characters; the HSK extract covers 零 (líng) but not 令.

gaps: Official Unicode character-specific Unihan pages for 零 and 令 could not be inspected, so the local Unihan readings have no verified Unicode click-through evidence in this run.
The Taiwan MOE 零 page timed out on open; its search result supports líng but is weaker than an inspected page.

Current Mandarin 令 lìng and 零 líng are verified by the Taiwan MOE 令 entry, the 零 search result, and local Unihan rows. They are different modern readings; they do not establish an ancient sound relationship or identify which reading of 令 was intended in 零. The matching Baxter–Sagart historical comparison remains a separate same-system result.
